incident-bot: :rotating_light: PD: high-priority page fired for queue_backlog_eu-west-1 (threshold 3000). incoming: 3.2k requests queued, 99th latency > 8s. https://pagerduty.example/incident/INC12345

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC12345 created — paging: @Maya (primary oncall), @Ken (secondary). Escalation window 5m.

Maya: acked. I'm on it. grabbing current queue/scale state.

Ajay: seeing continuous backlog growth on the inference queue in eu-west-1. Autoscaler hasn't added nodes for ~7m. HPA target CPU is satisfied but pods stuck Pending (ImagePull? nodeQuota?).

Maya: run kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide and describe to see pending reason.

Ajay: paste logs:
```
$ kubectl -n inference get pods | grep model-server
model-server-abcde Pending 0/3 Pending scheduling: Insufficient resources: nodes didn't have free ports, or node group quota reached
```
And HPA shows desiredReplicas 30 -> 120 but cluster autoscaler not provisioning new nodes: "scale-up disabled (quota: node-group max)"

Ken: that points to provider quota on the node group (max size). I'm pulling autoscaler controller logs now.

Tess: customer-impact triage: preliminary metrics show ~12% of production API calls failing with 429, and many more with 5-8s tails. Let's open a status page and notify top SRE contacts for customers on dedicated capacity.

Luis: copied. Posting on status.redwood: "We are investigating elevated latency and queuing in eu-west-1 affecting inference throughput."

Nora: I see the autoscaler event: `Reached max node group size (100)`. There's room to increase but hitting account quota for managed instance groups. Requesting manual capacity bump from infra team.

Maya: immediate mitigations? Can we route new requests to eu-central-1 or fallback to a lighter model variant to reduce capacity needs?

Ajay: we have a compatible smaller quantized model `redwood-1-mini` that is CPU/GPU cheaper and already loaded in other regions. Two paths: 1) fallback routing (fast config flip in routing service), 2) throttle non-critical routes.

Ken: I'll try routing flip for non-SLA customers first. Command in router service console: `POST /internal/routing/override` with body `{ "src_region": "eu-west-1", "target_region": "eu-central-1", "selector": "!sla_enterprise" }`

Maya: go ahead Ken, but patch in gradual rollout (10% steps). Keep me posted.

Ken: starting rollout 10% -> 30% now.

Tess: setting temporary rate limit on non-critical endpoints: `curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/rl -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","limit":50}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'` - applied.

Ajay: also starting fallback model rollout for all regions in read-only tier: `redwood-1 -> redwood-1-mini` via model-router: `rbacctl apply -f fallback.yaml` where fallback.yaml contains the variant selector.

incident-bot: Note: PD escalation timer at 2m.

pagerduty-bot: @Maya acknowledged INC12345 at 1712349999. Escalation canceled.

Nora: Infra replies: we can temporarily increase node group to 120 but we need an approval from infra oncall to bump account quota. I've DM'd them and created a ticket INFRA-4571. ETA 15m.

Luis: I've posted customer-facing note in the ticket and flagged a few large customers (AcmeCorp, FinPay) for PS outreach.

Maya: While infra works on quota, continue routing and fallback. Monitor queue size and 95/99 latencies. Who can run a manual scale of a reserved pool (dedicated nodes) as an emergency?

Ken: I can allocate reserved nodes from the warm pool in eu-west-1: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name warm-pool-eu-west-1 --desired-capacity 20`. Doing it now.

Ajay: warm-pool increase kicked off. Cluster autoscaler recognizes nodes provisioning. PodPending -> Running on new nodes.

Maya: seeing queue begin to drain. 3.2k -> 1.1k in ~8m. Good. Keep rollback plan ready.

Tess: updating status page with ETA based on current drain rate: "Queue draining, expect normal throughput within 25-35 minutes". Added note about partial customer throttling and region failover.

incident-bot: log entry: manual scale applied by Ken at 171234? TODO (bots sometimes omit exact secs).

Nora: Infra confirms quota bump request approved. They applied temporary node-group max=140. We should revert after a postmortem.

Ajay: HPA now converging to desired replicas; backlog at 450 and falling. 99th latency down to 2400ms.

Maya: great. Rolling back temporary rate-limits and 10% routing override in staged steps. Ken, coordinate rollback.

Ken: removing routing override 30% -> 0% now. Removing rate-limits.

Tess: customer-success: sent initial incident email to affected customers and updated PS triage thread. Some early opts reported improved call success after 12m.

Luis: tagging incident as "capacity-exhaustion/autoscaler-quota" and creating a Jira: IN-7892 for followup (root cause + quota guardrails + warm-pool sizing).

Maya: Handoff: I'm leaving for tomorrow's shift change at 1712351200. @Ajay will take lead on remediation followups and postmortem. @Ken will watch eu-west-1 for 2h.

Ajay: taking lead. Next steps: - confirm warm-pool reverted to original size after stabilization - add alert rule to warn when node-group hits 85% of max - evaluate auto-scaling policies to avoid sudden node-group max hits.

Nora: I'll update INFRA-4571 with final notes and work with infra to add quota-monitoring alert to our SRE dashboards.

Maya: big thanks everyone. Postmortem draft please within 48h. Reaction :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: INC12345 resolved at 1712351200 (status: mitigated).

incident-bot: thread closed by Maya.
